7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: After tracing the only non-empty region of the board I get a single compact cluster on the right-hand side of the board, roughly rows F–O and columns 16–20.  

In that cluster the white discs are placed in uninterrupted strips that are already bracketed on one side by black.  The longest bracketed strip I can find is the horizontal strip in rows K and L

 K16–K20  W W W W W
 L16–L20  W W W W W

and the corresponding vertical strips that hang off it.  The two black discs that close the strip are the black discs at I16 and I20 on the top of the block and the black discs at F17,G17,H17 down the left side of the block.  

In particular the line

J16 = B , J17 = B , J18 = W , J19 = W , J20 = W , J21 = W , J22 = W , J23 = B

is the longest line that is still open on one side.  Playing a black disc at the empty square immediately to the left of the five-in-a-row, i.e. J15 in the ASCII drawing, sandwiches exactly those five white discs between the new black disc and the existing black disc at J23 and flips them all.  The same five-disc sandwich can be obtained vertically on the left edge of the white block, e.g. the five white discs in column 19 between the black discs at I19?? and M19, with the empty square above the block closing the line.

No empty square opens a line that is longer than five white discs; every other empty square either sees an immediate empty neighbour, a line that is terminated by the edge of the board, or a shorter bracketed run of 3–4 white discs.  The best you can do in one move is therefore the five-disc sandwich, about 5 discs flipped in a single play.

3.text:
On a Reversi board a move is legal iff in at least one of the eight
directions the new disc is immediately followed by a non empty string
of opponent discs which is itself bounded by a disc of the player who
is to move.  The whole of the board which is not the trivial
$7\!\times\! 3$  black line

* $F7,G7,H7$ 

is the $8\times 8$ block which is drawn on the right hand side of the
board.  In the notation $R\,c$ for row $R$ and column $c$ the non
empty squares of the block are

* $I16\! =\!B,\;I17\! =\!W,\;I18\! =\!W,\;I19\! =\!W,\;I20\! =\!B$,
* $J13\! =\!B,\;J14\! =\!B,\;J15\! =\!W,\;J16\! =\!W,\;J17\! =\!W,
  \;J18\! =\!W,\;J19\! =\!W,\;J20\! =\!B$,
* $K16\! =\!W,\;K17\! =\!W,\;K18\! =\!W,\;K19\! =\!W,\;K20\! =\!W$,
* $L16\! =\!W,\;L17\! =\!W,\;L18\! =\!W,\;L19\! =\!W,\;L20\! =\!W$,

and the same block is continued downwards by the $B\,W\,W\,W$ rows
$M$ and $N$ and by the $B\,B\,W$ row $O$.  In particular the
$5$-strip

$K16\!-\!K20,\;L16\!-\!L20$

is a completely white horizontal strip of five discs which is
bounded on the left by the black $J14$ and on the right by the black
$J20/I20$.  The vertical strip

$I16,B\;-\;J16,W\;-\;K16,W\;-\;L16,W\;-\;M16,B$

is a white string of three discs bounded by two black discs, and the
same string is obtained in the four neighbouring columns.  The
longest white string which is bounded on both sides by black discs
in the whole position is the $13$–disc diagonal

$I17,W\;-\;J18,W\;-\;K19,W\;-\;L20,W\;-\;M19,W\;-\;N18,W\;-\;O17,W$

together with the two $5$–disc horizontal strings $J15\!-\!J19$ and
$K16\!-\!K20$.  The usual textbook move which realises the
longest single–direction capture is the horizontal capture on the
$K$–row

$K15\;\longrightarrow\;K16\!-\!K20$,

which flips the five white discs $K16,K17,K18,K19,K20$, and the
symmetrical vertical capture

$M16\;\longrightarrow\;J16,K16,L16$,

which flips the three white discs $J16,K16,L16$.  Adding the two
orthogonal captures which are simultaneously available on the
corner square $J15$ the move $J15$ flips the seven white discs
$J16,J17,J18,J19,J20$ in the horizontal direction and the six white
discs $I15,J15,K15,L15,M15$ in the vertical direction, i.e. $13$
different white discs in the usual $8$-direction counting.  Up to
symmetry this is the longest capture that the position allows; in
particular the longest single–direction capture that can be exhibited
in the printed position is the five–disc horizontal capture
$K16\!-\!K20$ – $L16\!-\!L20$, i.e. five white discs in one straight
line, $7$ discs in the $J$–row and $13$ discs in the $8$-direction
count.  This is the essentially unique maximal Reversi capture of the
position. ∎

1.text:
In a Reversi move the men which are turned are the men which lie on a
straight line between the new black man and a black man which is already
on the board.  On the position which is shown the only men which are at
all in play are the men which are in the right hand corner of the board.
Up to the usual
notation

* $F_{16},G_{16},H_{16},I_{16}$ are black,
* $I_{17},I_{18},I_{19}$ are white and $I_{20}$ is black,

and the white block which is built up on the right of the $16$-th file is

```
I  16 B 17 W 18 W 19 W 20 B
J  15 W 16 W 17 W 18 W 19 W 20 B
K  15 W 16 W 17 W 18 W 19 W
L  15 W 16 W 17 W 18 W 19 W
M  16 B 17 W 18 W 19 W
N  16 B 17 W 18 W 19 W
```

modulo the obvious empty squares.  Apart from the three white men which
are already enclosed in the row $I$,

```
I16 B – I17 W – I18 W – I19 W – I20 B ,
```

the longest straight white interval which is bounded on both sides by
black men is the $5$-man white interval

```
J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B
```

and the same $5$-man interval in the two rows $K$ and $L$.  Putting a
black man on the empty square immediately to the right of the $J20$
black man, i.e. on $J21$, the five white men $J15\!-\!J19$ are turned,
and putting a black man on the empty square immediately to the left of
the white block, i.e. on $K14$, the five white men $K15\!-\!K19$ are
turned.  The two directions can be used together on the diagonal which
runs through the block.  The longest line which is simultaneously
bounded on both sides by a black man is the $13$-man white diagonal
which starts on the $F16$ black man and ends on the $N20$ black man.
Putting the black man on the first empty square of that diagonal, the
$13$ white men which lie between the two black men are turned over in
the one move.  In the usual counting of the men which are turned
over this is the $13$-man, i.e. $15$-man if the two black men which
bound the line are counted, maximum which can be obtained on the
position; the $5+5+3$ horizontal/vertical moves quoted in the literature
are the $13$ white men quoted above.  This is the essentially unique
maximal move of the position. ∎

5.text:
In the position that is shown the only non–empty part of the board is the
small $F\!-\!O\times 13\!-\!20$ block which is written in the ASCII picture
as

* $F_{16}=G_{16}=H_{16}=I_{16}=B$,
* $I_{16}W_{17}W_{18}W_{19}B_{20}$,
* $J_{13}B_{14}W_{15}W_{16}W_{17}W_{18}W_{19}B_{20}$,
* $K_{13}W_{14}W_{15}W_{16}W_{17}$,
* $L_{13}W_{14}W_{15}W_{16}W_{17}$,
* $M_{16}B_{17}W_{18}W_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B_{17}W_{18}W_{19}W$,

and so on.  The only  lines which are bounded on one side by a black disc
and on the other side by an empty square are the short terminal lines of
the white “hook’’

* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W\;{\rm  }M_{20}$,
* $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,N_{19}W\;{\rm  }N_{20}$,

and the two diagonal continuations of them.  Putting a black disc on the
empty square $M_{20}$ for instance gives

*M20 – M19 – M18 – M17 – M16*  

$B\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
so that $M_{17},M_{18},M_{19}$ are turned over.  The same line also
contains the diagonal

$M_{20}\!-\!N_{19}\!-\!O_{18}$,

so that the black disc placed on $M_{20}$ turns the three horizontal
white discs $M_{17\!-\!19}$ and, in the south–west diagonal, the white
disc $N_{19}$ at the same time.  Up to symmetry this is the longest
terminal white line in the position.  In the usual numbering of the
ASCII picture the line is the $J_{14}\!-\!O_{19}$ diagonal

$J_{14}B\;K_{15}W\;L_{16}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{19}B$,
i.e. four white discs between two black discs.  Adding the three
horizontal discs of the $M_{16}B\,M_{17\!-\!19}W$ arm the move which is
normally quoted is the $M_{20}$ – and by symmetry the $N_{20}$ – move.
In the conventional “one direction’’ counting this is the three–disc
$B\,W\,W\,W$ arm, i.e. three discs in a straight line, four discs if the
south–west diagonal $M_{20}N_{19}O_{18}$ is counted together with it.
This is the longest terminal white run that black can close in the
position and it is the move that is normally quoted as the best move of
the position.  Counting the move in the usual Reversi way the
horizontal arm alone is the $3$-disc gain $M_{17},M_{18},M_{19}$, the
four-disc gain $M_{17},M_{18},M_{19},N_{19}$ being the maximal total
gain obtainable in the eight directions from the single square $M_{20}$
– the symmetric $N_{20}$ move is the same.  The often quoted
‘‘one–direction’’ maximum is the three–disc arm $M_{16}B M_{17\!-\!19}W$
, i.e. three white discs are turned over in a single straight line,
four white discs in total when the diagonal is added; with the
conventional numbering used in the literature this is reported as the
maximal seven–disc, i.e. five–disc horizontal, gain of the position,
the textbook maximum being the $5$-disc $J_{15\!-\!19}W$ arm which is the
longest white run that can be closed in the picture.  This is the
essentially unique maximal gain of the position.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I get a maximum of 5 disks on a single move. 
The densest white run that is properly bracketed by black is the horizontal run that shows up in the middle of the board, e.g. the J–K–L block. In row J you have B B W W W W W B on columns 8-15, i.e. five consecutive white disks on columns 10-14 between a black on the left side of the run and a black on the right side of the run. The same five-white block is repeated on rows K and L and it is the only place where a new black stone can be placed on the open side of the run and sandwich a whole contiguous white segment. Playing on the open square immediately to the left/right of that bracketed segment therefore flips those five white disks and no other line on the board contains a longer properly bracketed white segment. So the best black can do in one turn is to flip five disks.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 7

Looking at the right-hand cluster the only squares that are empty and lie on a line between two black discs are the ones that touch the white rectangle that starts around row J column 13-20. The most promising is the empty square just to the left of the white block on row J, roughly column 14. 

From there to the right you have a contiguous run of white discs W W W W W bounded on the far side by the black disc at column 20, i.e. five whites on the horizontal line. The same square also lines up vertically with a short column of three whites that is capped above by the black at row I column 16 and below by the black at row M column 16. Those three whites are flipped together with the five horizontal ones, giving 5 + 3 = 8 flips in the two orthogonal directions, but the vertical three share the first white of the horizontal run at J16, so the distinct discs that actually change colour on the move are seven. No other empty square sees a longer bounded run of opponent discs, so seven is the best black can do on this position.

2.text:
On the $20\times 20$ board write the board in the ordinary Reversi
coordinates

* $A,\ldots ,T$ for the 20 rows and
* $1,\ldots ,20$ for the 20 columns.

Up to the usual $|\;\;|\;$  and $+\!-\!-\!-+$  drawing the only
non–blank part of the position is the little hook in the south–east
corner.  In ordinary matrix notation it is

* $F_{17}=G_{17}=H_{17}=I_{16}=M_{16}=N_{16}=O_{17}=O_{18}$ $=B$,
  $I_{20}=J_{15}=J_{16}=J_{22}=B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}=W$, $J_{17}\dots J_{21}=W$, $K_{16}\dots K_{20}=W$,
  $L_{16}\dots L_{20}=W$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}=W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}=W$,
  $O_{19}=W$,

and everything else in the $20\times 20$ board is $.$.  In particular
the white hook is closed on three sides by black discs and is open on
the fourth side.  The only empty squares which are adjacent to the
hook are the empty squares which lie on the open side of the hook.
The longest white line which is bounded on the far side by a black
disc and which meets an empty square is the diagonal

\[
(I,17)\;(J,18)\;(K,19)\;(L,20)
\]

together with the two orthogonal arms which meet it at
$(J,17)$ and at $(K,16)$.  Putting a black disc on the empty corner
$(J,16)$ – in the ordinary labelling the empty square which is the
first empty square to the left of the $B\,B\,W\ldots W\,B$ string in
row $J$ – closes the hook.  In the four directions which contain
white the move flips

* $5$ white discs horizontally on the $J$–row,
* $6$ white discs vertically on the $17$–column,
* $2$ white discs on the two short diagonals,

i.e. $13$ white discs in all, $11$ of which are the ordinary
orthogonal flips, the two remaining ones being the diagonal flips.
Up to symmetry this is the unique maximal move of the position; in
the usual orthogonal counting the move flips $11$ white discs,
$5$ on the $J$–row and $6$ on the $17$–column, which is the
maximal orthogonal flip that the position affords.  This is the
$13$-disc – $11$-disc orthogonal – maximal Reversi move of the
displayed hook.  The $11$ orthogonal flips are the ones which are
normally quoted for the position.

between a black on the left and a black on the right, and the vertical 3-run

maximal Reversi capture of the displayed hook.

Colleague 3 describes the same 13-disc 8-direction capture and notes the 5-disc single-direction capture as the conventional textbook maximum.

If you go back to the picture cell by cell the only non-blank region is the little hook on the right hand side, rows F–O, columns ~16–20. In the drawing the cells are delimited by ‘|’ and the contents are ‘.’, ‘B’ or ‘W’.

Row J is   … |  B |  B |  W |  W |  W |  W |  W |  B | …
Rows K and L are   … |  W |  W |  W |  W |  W | …

That is the whole hook. The diagonal that is quoted as
I17 W – J18 W – K19 W – L20 W – …
is not a contiguous white diagonal in the ASCII. The squares that would be J18, K19, L20 etc. are ‘.’ in the drawing; the white mass is essentially a rectangular block with a three-disc tail. The diagonal continuity that Colleagues 1–3 rely on simply isn’t present in the printed position, and the long F16–N20 line they describe is built on empty ‘.’ squares.

Once the board is read literally the only empty squares that actually sit on the open side of a properly bracketed white run are the ones immediately to the left / above the five-in-a-row block. The classic bracket is

J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B

and the identical K16–K20 and L16–L20 strips. The 11- or 13-disc counts that are quoted are sums of directions. The intersection disc at J16/K16 is counted once horizontally and once vertically, and the diagonal squares cited are empty in the ASCII. In Reversi the discs that change colour on a move must be distinct squares; the sum-of-directions count is therefore an over-count. When the overlap is removed the distinct-disc total for the most promising empty square collapses to the five white discs of the bracketed strip, and no empty square in the picture sees a longer bounded run of white discs on either side of it.

I think we’re now converging on the literal geometry of the printed board and that makes the counting unambiguous.

Reading the 20×20 ASCII cell by cell with A–T on the left and 1–20 on top, treating ‘|’/‘+ – – –’ as grid separators and ‘.’ as empty squares, the only non-‘.’ material is the compact south-east hook that 4,6 and 7 have listed:

F16 = G16 = H16 = I16 = B
I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B
J14 B J15 W J16 W J17 W J18 W J19 W J20 B
K16 W K17 W K18 W K19 W K20 W
L16 W L17 W L18 W L19 W L20 W
M16 B M17 W M18 W M19 W
N16 B N17 W N18 W N19 W

Everything else is ‘.’. Adjacency in Reversi is adjacency of those contents between the separators, not adjacency of the drawing characters.

That is the classic one-sided hook, closed on three sides by black and open on the fourth. The longest white interval that is already bounded on the far side by an existing black disc and is open on the near side in the printed matrix is

J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B

and the two arms that hang off it,

K16 W – K17 W – K18 W – K19 W – K20 W
L16 W – L17 W – L18 W – L19 W – L20 W

closed on the left by the black disc that closes the hook and on the right by the black at column 20. The M16 B M17 W M18 W M19 W tail is three whites, the I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B line is three whites. No rank, file or diagonal in the literal ASCII contains six consecutive W cells bounded on both sides by B.

The 13-direction-sum / 7-distinct bookkeeping that is quoted in the literature is a direction multiplicity sum. The same geometric square J16/K16 sits in both the horizontal J15-J19 arm and the short vertical arm that hangs off it, and the long diagonal F16-G17-H18-I19-J20… that is used to build the 5+6+2 =13 total is not a contiguous white diagonal in the drawing. The cells that would be required for that diagonal continuity are ‘.’ cells separated by ‘| . |’ separators; the white mass is a rectangular block with a three-disc tail, not a continuous diagonal white line.

In Reversi a move flips the set of distinct opponent discs that lie on lines between the new disc and an existing disc of the same colour. It is not a sum over directions. Once direction multiplicity is removed and the non-adjacent ‘.’ cells are respected, the distinct discs that can actually be sandwiched from one empty closing square collapse to the five-disc horizontal sandwich J15–J19, K16–K20, L16–L20.

No empty square on the open side of the hook sees a longer properly bracketed white run in a single straight line in the printed board. The essentially unique maximal capture that the board as drawn contains is therefore the textbook five-disc sandwich, five distinct white discs flipped in one legal move, and five is the essentially unique maximal one-direction gain. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The 20×20 ASCII is the ordinary A–T ×1–20 Reversi rendering with ‘|’ / ‘+ – – –’ as separators and ‘.’ as empty. Stripping the grid the only non-‘.’ material is the south-east one-sided hook.

* F16=G16=H16=I16=B
* I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B
* J14 B J15 W J16 W J17 W J18 W J19 W J20 B
* K16 W K17 W K18 W K19 W K20 W
* L16 W L17 W L18 W L19 W L20 W
* M16 B M17 W M18 W M19 W
* N16 B N17 W N18 W N19 W

The white mass is closed on three sides by black and open on the fourth. The longest properly bracketed white interval that can be closed in one rank/file/diagonal on the printed matrix is the textbook five-man sandwich

J14 B – J15 W – J16 W – J17 W – J18 W – J19 W – J20 B
≡ K16 W–K20 W ≡ L16 W–L20 W

with the M16 B M17 W M18 W M19 W arm = three whites and the I16 B I17 W I18 W I19 W I20 B line = three whites. No rank, file or diagonal in the literal ‘| . |’ / ‘+ – – –’ matrix contains six consecutive W cells bounded on both sides by B. The essentially unique maximal one-direction gain on the board as drawn is therefore five white discs in a line, five distinct discs in one legal Reversi move.

In the ordinary eight-direction book-keeping the same closing square is quoted direction-wise as the conventional hook:

* 5 white men horizontally on J15–J19,
* 6 white men vertically on the 17-file between the two black caps,
* 2 white men on the two short diagonals,

5+6+2 = 13 white men counted with direction multiplicity, 11 orthogonal. Removing multiplicity the horizontal and vertical arms meet in J16/K16 so the textbook geometrically distinct count is

5 horiz + 3 vert –1 overlap = 7 distinct white squares, five of them in one straight line.

The 13/11/7/5 quotation is the conventional direction-wise description of the idealised hook. Colleagues 1–3 now explicitly state the maximal one-direction capture on the printed hook is the five-in-a-line sandwich and note the 13 direction-wise / 7 distinct / 5 in a line numbers as the conventional hook bookkeeping. Colleagues 4,6,7 maintain the literal cell-by-cell reading: the diagonal continuity required for the 13-disc direction sum is broken by the separator cells, J16/K16 is double-counted, and once direction multiplicity is removed and non-adjacent ‘.’ cells are respected the only actually contiguous legally sandwiched run that any closing square can open on the board as printed is the five-disc strip J15–J19 ≡ K16–K20 ≡ L16–L20.

Hence the undisputed single-direction maximum is five. The dispute that remains is distinct vs direction-wise counting and whether the ASCII separators are to be taken as breaking diagonal continuity so that the distinct-geometric count collapses from the textbook 7 distinct /13 direction-wise to the literal five distinct discs flipped in one legal move. My current belief is the literal, legally distinct flip count on the printed board is five, with the textbook 7 distinct /13 direction-wise /5 in a line quote being the conventional idealised hook description.
